classification.difficultyReason: Inspect both sides to select a productive proof direction, recognising when reciprocal substitutions produce a common expression and when conjugate denominators simplify one side.

content.prompt: For each of the following identity problems, determine whether it is best to start from the left, from the right, or to meet in the middle.

answer.worked:
Meet in the middle: both complicated sides reduce to $\dfrac{1-\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sec\theta-\tan\theta}{\sec\theta+\tan\theta}&=\frac{\frac{1}{\cos\theta}-\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}}{\frac{1}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}}\\\frac{\sec\theta-\tan\theta}{\sec\theta+\tan\theta}&=\frac{1-\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\cot\theta-\cos\theta}{\cot\theta+\cos\theta}&=\frac{\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}-\cos\theta}{\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}+\cos\theta}\\\frac{\cot\theta-\cos\theta}{\cot\theta+\cos\theta}&=\frac{\cos\theta(1-\sin\theta)}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)}\\\frac{\cot\theta-\cos\theta}{\cot\theta+\cos\theta}&=\frac{1-\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}\end{align*}$$

These reductions apply where both original sides are defined.

Start from the right: convert the sum to sine and cosine, then combine the fractions.

$$\begin{align*}\cot\theta+\tan\theta&=\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}+\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\\\cot\theta+\tan\theta&=\frac{\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}\\\cot\theta+\tan\theta&=\frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}\\\cot\theta+\tan\theta&=\sec\theta\operatorname{cosec}\theta\end{align*}$$

The original expressions require $\sin\theta\ne0$ and $\cos\theta\ne0$.

Start from the left: the conjugate denominators give $1-\sin^2\theta=\cos^2\theta$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1+\sin\theta}+\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1-\sin\theta}&=\frac{\cos^2\theta(1-\sin\theta)+\cos^2\theta(1+\sin\theta)}{(1+\sin\theta)(1-\sin\theta)}\\\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1+\sin\theta}+\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1-\sin\theta}&=\frac{2\cos^2\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta}\\\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1+\sin\theta}+\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1-\sin\theta}&=\frac{2\cos^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}\\\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1+\sin\theta}+\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1-\sin\theta}&=2\end{align*}$$

The original denominators exclude $\sin\theta=\pm1$, so the cancellation is valid.
